string.text: {=taom_str_culture_description.empire}The Dunlendings, fierce hillmen of the western highlands, are a proud and ancient people. Resentful of the Rohirrim, they are known for their guerilla tactics and tenacity in battle. United under strong leaders, they fight for their survival and to reclaim the lands they believe are rightfully theirs.

{=taom_str_culture_description.vlandia}The Rohirrim, known as the Horse-lords, are the proud and noble people of Rohan, a realm of wide open plains and rolling hills. They are renowned for their skill as riders and their unmatched cavalry, which forms the backbone of their military strength. Living in a tightly-knit feudal society, the Rohirrim are led by a king and a loyal nobility who are bound by honor and tradition to protect their land and people. They are fiercely independent, valuing freedom above all, and their warriors are trained to fight with spears, swords, and bows, all while astride their powerful steeds.

{=taom_str_culture_description.battania}The Variags of Khand are a ruthless and warlike people from the eastern steppes. Known for their mastery of horses and deadly chariots, they bring a unique and brutal style of warfare. Aligned with Sauron, the Variags fight for power and plunder, spreading fear across Middle-earth.

{=taom_str_culture_description.khuzait}The Easterlings are a proud and disciplined people, hailing from the vast eastern lands beyond Mordor. Renowned for their resilience and mastery of warfare, they are both farmers and warriors, blending agrarian traditions with a fierce martial culture. Their armies are known for their fearsome cavalry, adorned in ornate armor and carrying deadly spears and bows. With a rich heritage of craftsmanship and loyalty to their kin, the Easterlings march to war under vibrant banners of gold and crimson, striking fear into the hearts of their enemies. Their allegiance to Sauron has made them a formidable force, uniting under his shadow to expand their dominion across Middle-earth.

{=taom_str_culture_description.aserai}The Haradrim, warriors of the southern deserts, are a fierce and resilient people allied with Sauron. Known for their exotic war beasts and skilled cavalry, they march to war under crimson banners. Proud and deeply rooted in their traditions, they bring the savagery of the desert to the battlefields of Middle-earth.

{=taom_str_culture_description.sturgia}The Bardings of Dale, descendants of Bard the Bowman, are a proud and industrious people living in the shadow of Erebor. Renowned for their skilled archers and disciplined warriors, they safeguard their thriving city and the trade routes of the north. United by a strong sense of community and honor, the Bardings stand firm against the darkness threatening their lands.

{=taom_str_culture_description.erebor}The noble Dwarves of Erebor, are renowned for their craftsmanship, resilience, and pride. From their halls in the Lonely Mountain, they forge mighty weapons and treasures of unmatched beauty. Clad in mail and armed with axes, they defend their kin with steadfast courage, seeking to reclaim their legacy and preserve their heritage against all who threaten it.

{=taom_str_culture_description.rivendell}Rivendell, the Last Homely House, is a refuge of wisdom and beauty led by Lord Elrond. Nestled in the Misty Mountains, its people are loremasters and guardians of Middle-earth's ancient knowledge. The Elves of Rivendell offer counsel and aid to those who stand against the darkness, preserving the light of hope and unity.

{=taom_str_culture_description.mirkwood}The Wood-Elves of Mirkwood, led by King Thranduil, are guardians of the vast and mysterious forest. Known for their agility and mastery of the bow, they blend into the shadows, striking with precision and grace. Their realm is one of beauty and peril, protected by the resolve of its warriors and the timeless wisdom of their king. Fiercely independent, the Elves of Mirkwood fight to preserve their forest against encroaching darkness.

{=taom_str_culture_description.lothlorien}The Galadhrim of Lothlórien, dwellers of the Golden Wood, are an ethereal and noble people led by Lady Galadriel and Lord Celeborn. Masters of archery and woodland warfare, they guard their enchanted realm with unmatched skill. Their loyalty to their kin and homeland is unwavering, and their subtle magic preserves Lothlórien as a sanctuary of hope and light amidst the growing shadow.

{=taom_str_culture_description.isengard}The armies of Isengard, led by Saruman the White, are a formidable force of Uruk-hai and mercenaries. Forged in the fires of industry, their weapons and armor are crafted for destruction. The forces of Isengard march to war with ruthless efficiency, bent on conquest and domination.

{=taom_str_culture_description.gundabad}The Orcs of Gundabad, residing in the mist-shrouded mountains, are a brutal and savage force. Led by their warlords, they wage endless raids on neighboring lands. Driven by hatred and cruelty, they are relentless in their quest to dominate the north.

{=taom_str_culture_description.umbar}The Corsairs of Umbar, seafaring raiders and master sailors, are a ruthless and cunning people allied with Sauron. Known for their swift ships and relentless naval warfare, they strike fear into the coastlines of Middle-earth. Proud of their maritime heritage, they bring the chaos of the seas to the land, raiding and pillaging in the name of their dark alliances.

{=taom_str_culture_description.dolguldur}The minions of Dol Guldur, under the command of the Necromancer, are a dark and sinister force. Hidden within the corrupted forest of Mirkwood, they employ treachery and shadow to weaken their enemies. Orcs, wargs, and other foul creatures march forth to spread fear and decay across Middle-earth.

{=taom_str_culture_description.gondor}The Gondorians, descendants of the Númenórean exiles, are the proud stewards of the greatest kingdom of Men in Middle-earth. Known for their towering stone fortresses and unwavering courage, Gondor is a bastion of hope against the looming shadow of Mordor. Its disciplined armies, comprised of valiant infantry, skilled archers, and mounted knights, stand as a shield for all free peoples. Guided by noble stewards and captains, the Gondorians hold fast to their traditions, unyielding in their duty to protect the realm and its legacy.

{=taom_str_culture_description.mordor}The armies of Mordor, forged in the shadow of Mount Doom, are a relentless force of darkness commanded by Sauron, the Dark Lord. Comprised of orcs, trolls, and wicked men, they march to war under the burning Eye, sowing fear and destruction. These legions are driven by cruelty and servitude, wielding jagged blades and crude armor. Bound by Sauron's iron will, the forces of Mordor are a deadly tide seeking to engulf all of Middle-earth in shadow.

{=taom_shaghana_desc}Shaghâna is the eastern reach of Harad, a land of sun-scorched steppes and ancient fortresses. Its nine tribal clans are fierce warriors, bound together by oath and blood, striking fear into those who dare oppose them.

{=aom_shaghana_desc}The Shaghâna are a fierce tribal people of the eastern Harad steppes, renowned as relentless raiders and skilled horsemen. Bound by oath and clan, they answer to their Taskral and serve the dark designs of Sauron from their sun-scorched fortresses.

{=taom_abanissa_desc}Âbanissa lies in the deep south of Harad, a realm of humid jungles and ancient stone dynasties. The great Houses of Âbanissa command fearsome war-beasts and armies of disciplined warriors, their power answerable to none but Sauron himself.

{=aom_abanissa_desc}The great Houses of Âbanissa rule the deep south of Harad, a land of humid jungles, ancient stone palaces and towering war-beasts. Their armies march beneath banners of dynasty, commanding respect and terror across the southern lands.

{=TAOM_ghilman_text}The Serpent Guard are mounted soldiers in the service of the Serpentlord of Near Harad. Bred in the saddle on the rolling plains south of the Ephel Dúath, they are unmatched as horse-archers in all of Middle-earth's southern lands. In times of peace between Harad and Mordor, the Guard hires its services to Haradrim lords and to any other power rich enough to afford their golden fee.

{=TAOM_legion_text}The Grey Company are the last organised brotherhood of the Dúnedain Rangers, descendants of the kings of Arnor who lost their kingdom ages ago. They ride across the North without a home of their own, keeping the peace in lands that have forgotten their names. Though their first loyalty is to the line of Elendil, they take contracts from lords across Middle-earth when their wandering brings them through civilised lands.

{=TAOM_skolderbrotva_text}The Axemen of Erebor are veterans of King Thorin's battles who found peacetime ill-suited to their temperament. Trained in the close-quarter fighting of the Dwarven halls — shield wall, short axe, mattock — they are formidable on any terrain but excel in the mountain passes that connect Erebor to the kingdoms of men. They take contracts from any who can afford their fee, but will not raise an axe against Erebor or Rivendell.

{=TAOM_company_text}The Corsair Blades are veteran sea-fighters from the harbours of Umbar who have taken to selling their skills on land. They fight as crossbowmen — the preferred arm of shipboard warfare — and are as comfortable in a siege as they are on a rolling deck. Their captain, a scarred Númenórean exile, keeps them to their contracts with iron discipline, knowing that their reputation is their most valuable cargo.

{=TAOM_beni_zilal_text}The Blind Eye is a brotherhood of smugglers, fences, and hired killers operating across the coasts of Harad and the deep desert. They are said to descend from a cult of assassins who served a forgotten Haradrim king, and their methods — poison, shadow, and the leveraging of secrets — remain unchanged. Lords who wish to quietly remove a rival, or merchants who need cargo moved without customs inspection, know where to leave a gold coin and a sealed letter.

{=TAOM_wolfskins_text}The Variag Ravagers are war-bands of young Variag warriors from the steppes of Khand who spend their early manhood in a state of ritual warfare: they may own no cooked food, sleep under no permanent roof, and take no mercy. While most eventually return to the settled life of their clans, some never do, and these form the Ravagers — outlaws who prey on the roads of Khand and raid across its borders into Harad and Gondor.

{=TAOM_brotherhood_text}The Dunlending Reavers are the broken remnant of a hill-clan that once dwelt in the valleys now ruled by the Rohirrim. Their grandfathers were driven from fertile land into the rocky heights, and they have nursed that bitterness into a raider's philosophy: everything taken from a southron or a king's man is merely the restoration of what was stolen. In practice they are brigands, but dangerous ones who know every goat-track through the hills.

{=TAOM_hidden_hand_text}The Mouth's Servants are the Eyes of Barad-dûr operating beyond the Black Gate — informants, enforcers, and spies embedded among the peoples bordering Mordor. Where Sauron's armies cannot yet reach, these agents collect tribute and silence dissent. They work through bribery, blackmail, and quiet murder, ensuring that no conspiracy against the Dark Lord takes root before it is uprooted and crushed.

{=TAOM_lakepike_text}The Wreckers of the Long Lake live in the reed-beds and rotting old jetties of the Long Lake's shadowed shores, far from the respectable lights of Esgaroth. They make their living by luring barges onto hidden shoals with false lanterns, then stripping the cargo and selling it through fences in the town itself. Despite the efforts of the Lake-town Master and the Dale merchants, the Wreckers have too many friends in the dockside taverns to be easily driven out.

{=TAOM_embers_text}The Cult of the Lidless Eye is a secret society rooted in the Black Númenórean tradition, venerating Sauron as a god-king who will restore his faithful to glory when he rises again. They recruit among the dispossessed of Dunland and the forgotten corners of the realm, promising divine favour and earthly power. In truth, their leaders answer to agents of Barad-dûr, and their cell-based structure makes them nearly impossible for any lord's justice to eradicate.

{=TAOM_jawwal_text}The Sand-Riders are the nomadic desert clans of the deep Harad interior, masters of the waterless wastes between the Ephel Dúath and the distant southern sea. They range across routes known only to themselves, demanding tribute from any caravan bold enough to cross their territory. The settled lords of Near Harad treat them as a nuisance; the Sand-Riders consider the settled lords thieves who stole what the desert had already given freely.

{=TAOM_karakhuzaits_text}The Wild Easterlings are the unconquered steppe clans of the Sea of Rhûn, who have resisted the authority of every lord who has tried to bring them to heel — Rhûn chieftain, Mordor lieutenant, and King of Dale alike. They range across the grasslands east of the Celduin, rounding up horses, raiding flocks, and collecting road tribute from any caravan foolish enough to cross their steppe without an armed escort.

{=TAOM_forest_people_text}The Drúedain, known to Men as Woses or the Wild Men of the Woods, are an ancient people who dwell in the deep forest of Drúadan and the hidden valleys of the White Mountains. They clear ground with fire, grow what they need on the ash-rich soil, and move on when the land is spent — a way of life the settled peoples of Middle-earth have never understood and never bothered to. The Drúedain want no lord, pay no tax, and ask only to be left to the forest's silence.

{=TAOM_eleftheroi_text}The Beornings are the great woodmen who dwell in the vale of the Anduin between the Misty Mountains and Mirkwood, led by the skin-changers of Beorn's line. They allow no Orc to cross their territory, charge a toll at the Ford of Carrock to fund their watch, and answer to no king in Middle-earth. Though they will trade and talk with Elves and Dwarves, any army that marches through their forest without leave will find that the Beornings have very large teeth.

{=taom_hideout_desc_dunland}Among the wooded hills of Dunland you spy a rough camp of hide tents and a crude palisade, half-hidden in a clearing.
{=taom_hideout_desc_gundabad}Beneath the crags of the Misty Mountains you find a foul warren of Gundabad orcs burrowed into the bare rock.
{=taom_hideout_desc_harad}Out among the dunes of Harad you come upon a camouflaged Southron camp gathered about a hidden desert well.
{=taom_hideout_desc_rhun}On the wide grasslands of Rhûn you make out the wagons and hide-tents of an Easterling raiding band camped in a gully.
{=taom_hideout_desc_umbar}Along the southern shore you find a sheltered cove where the black ships of the Corsairs of Umbar lie at anchor.
{=taom_hideout_desc_erebor}Among the bleak hills of the east you come upon a dwarf-camp of the Blacklocks, a clan long ago fallen into shadow and ruin.
{=taom_faction_anduin_vale_desc}The fertile valley of the Great River Anduin, home to the Beornings and Woodmen. Simple folk who live between the Misty Mountains and Mirkwood.
{=taom_faction_aru_thani_of_bellakar_desc}The coastal realm of Bellakar, settled by Numenorean Faithful who remained true to the Valar. A bastion of civilization on the southern shores.

{=taom_faction_clans_of_dunland_desc}The Hill-Men of Dunland, ancient enemies of the Rohirrim. Battanian forest traditions blend with TAOM's Hill Marchers and Hill-Tribe Levies — cheap, fast, angry warbands that march on plain and forest alike. Battanian smiths are slow, but warbands are not.

{=taom_faction_goblins_of_blue_craig_perk_1_desc}+10% party speed on snow — goblins know every crag and tunnel.
{=taom_faction_goblins_of_blue_craig_perk_2_desc}The horde devours everything — +20% party food consumption.
{=taom_faction_goblins_of_blue_craig_su_0_desc}Numberless bow-armed rabble of the high crags.

{=taom_faction_goblins_of_goblin_town_desc}The teeming goblin-warrens beneath the High Pass of the Misty Mountains. Since the fall of the Great Goblin the tribes have multiplied without number — vast, ill-armed swarms that win by sheer weight and breed faster than any foe can cull them. They run swiftest over the snows of their mountain home, but such hordes are ever ravenous.
{=taom_faction_goblins_of_goblin_town_perk_0_desc}+40% party size and +25% village volunteer respawn — goblins are weak but numberless.
{=taom_faction_goblins_of_goblin_town_perk_1_desc}+10% party speed on snow — goblins know every pass and tunnel of the Misty Mountains.
{=taom_faction_goblins_of_goblin_town_perk_2_desc}Such a horde devours everything — +20% party food consumption.
{=taom_faction_goblins_of_goblin_town_su_0_desc}Massed spear-fodder of the High Pass warrens.
{=taom_faction_golden_realm_of_rhun_bonus_2}-10% mounted recruit and upgrade cost (Khuzait, inherited)
{=taom_faction_golden_realm_of_rhun_bonus_3}+25% horse, mule, cow, and sheep village production (Khuzait, inherited)

{=taom_faction_golden_realm_of_rhun_desc}The Easterlings of the eastern plains. Inherited Khuzait cavalry traditions paired with TAOM's Easterling Outriders steppe speed and Easterling Host party size. Heavy cavalry that arrives in numbers and tribute.
{=taom_faction_golden_realm_of_rhun_perk_0_desc}+10% party speed on steppe — riders of the Sea of Rhun cross the plain fast.
{=taom_faction_golden_realm_of_rhun_perk_1_desc}+5% party size limit — hordes muster in answer to Mordor's call.
{=taom_faction_golden_realm_of_rhun_perk_2_desc}Inherited Khuzait -10% mounted cost, +25% animal village production; -20% town tax income.

{=taom_faction_havens_of_umbar_desc}The corsair haven and Black Numenorean port-city on the southern bays. Corsair Trade slashes caravan costs, Corsair Glory adds renown, Desert Corsairs march fast across the sands — but Corsair Greed inflates every wage bill.
{=taom_faction_havens_of_umbar_perk_0_desc}-25% caravan cost and +15% tariff income — Umbar prospers on every passing ship.
{=taom_faction_havens_of_umbar_perk_1_desc}+8% renown per battle — the corsair name is sung in every port.
{=taom_faction_havens_of_umbar_perk_2_desc}+10% party speed on desert — Umbar's marches cross sand as easily as sea.

{=taom_faction_high_kingdom_of_lindon_desc}The green land west of the Blue Mountains, last realm of the High Elves on the shores of Middle-earth. From the Grey Havens of Mithlond the white ships sail into the West. Círdan the Shipwright, eldest of the Eldar, keeps the fading light of the Falathrim — wise, few, and each blade irreplaceable. Lindon shares the Falathrim strength of Mithlond.
{=taom_faction_high_kingdom_of_lindon_perk_0_desc}+35% influence awarded on army success — the Wise know how to lead.
{=taom_faction_high_kingdom_of_lindon_perk_1_desc}+20% village hearth growth and -15% party food consumption.
{=taom_faction_high_kingdom_of_lindon_perk_2_desc}+10% party speed in forest and +0.5 settlement loyalty per day.
{=taom_faction_high_kingdom_of_lindon_strength_1}Wise leadership reaps greater influence from victory
{=taom_faction_high_kingdom_of_lindon_su_2_desc}Heavy Falathrim guardian of the Grey Havens.
{=taom_faction_khudorom_of_khand_bonus_1}50% less forest speed penalty + 15% sight range (Battanian, inherited)
{=taom_faction_khudorom_of_khand_bonus_2}+20% chance for veteran militia in towns (Battanian, inherited)

{=taom_faction_khudorom_of_khand_desc}The Variag of Khand. Battanian forest militia traditions inherited; TAOM's Steppe Charioteers add +10% party speed on steppe on top. Mercenary bands ride for whoever pays the most coin.
{=taom_faction_khudorom_of_khand_perk_0_desc}+10% party speed on steppe — Variag chariots roll fast.
{=taom_faction_khudorom_of_khand_perk_1_desc}Mercenary captains ride for whoever pays — but they keep their cut.
{=taom_faction_khudorom_of_khand_perk_2_desc}Inherited 50% less forest speed penalty + 15% sight range and +20% chance for veteran militia in towns; -10% construction speed.
{=taom_faction_khudorom_of_khand_weakness_2}Mercenary captains are loyal to coin, not lord
{=taom_faction_kingdom_of_arthedain_desc}The last and greatest of the successor kingdoms of Arnor. Arthedain held out longest against the Witch-king of Angmar before its final fall.
{=taom_faction_kingdom_of_cardolan_desc}The successor realm of Cardolan, once part of the great kingdom of Arnor. Now a land of scattered settlements and ancient barrows haunted by wights.
{=taom_faction_kingdom_of_dale_bonus_3}+20% relationship penalty from kingdom decisions (Sturgian, inherited)
{=taom_faction_kingdom_of_dale_bonus_6}-0.5 settlement loyalty per day (Small Territory Exposure)

{=taom_faction_kingdom_of_dale_desc}Bard's rebuilt city beneath Erebor. Inherited Sturgian grain abundance and Sturgian cheap-army tradition pair with TAOM's Vale Traders plain-speed bonus — but Sturgian kingdom-decision penalties cut both ways. A thriving trade alliance with the Dwarves keeps Dale rich and ready.
{=taom_faction_kingdom_of_dale_perk_0_desc}+10% party speed on plains — caravans of Lake-town move fast.
{=taom_faction_kingdom_of_dale_perk_1_desc}Trade with Erebor provides bonus income and arms-supply.
{=taom_faction_kingdom_of_dale_perk_2_desc}Inherited Sturgian +10% village grain and -50% army influence cost; relationship penalty +20% on kingdom decisions.
{=taom_faction_kingdom_of_dorwinion_desc}The wine-growing realm of Dorwinion on the northwestern shores of the Sea of Rhun. A prosperous trading kingdom caught between the Free Peoples and the East.

{=taom_faction_kingdom_of_erebor_desc}The Lonely Mountain reclaimed. Master Smiths cut smithing energy by 30%; Dwarven Honor adds loyalty every day; Dwarven Stubbornness keeps morale unshakable. Slow to build a wall — but the wall holds until the mountain itself falls.
{=taom_faction_kingdom_of_erebor_perk_0_desc}-30% smithing energy cost — Dwarven forges work twice as fast.
{=taom_faction_kingdom_of_erebor_perk_1_desc}-25% garrison wage and +1 settlement loyalty per day.
{=taom_faction_kingdom_of_erebor_perk_2_desc}+5 party morale and +10% village production — Dwarves do not bend.
{=taom_faction_kingdom_of_ered_duin_desc}The Dwarven mansions of the Blue Mountains, ancestral halls of Durin's Folk. After the loss of Erebor, many Dwarves found refuge here before Thorin's quest.
{=taom_faction_kingdom_of_imladris_bonus_1}+20% village hearth growth (The Last Homely House)

{=taom_faction_kingdom_of_imladris_desc}Elrond's hidden valley, sanctuary of the Wise. Elven Wisdom unifies armies at little influence cost; the Last Homely House grows hearths in every village. Elven Pride still drives every council — every Noldor blade is irreplaceable.
{=taom_faction_kingdom_of_imladris_perk_0_desc}+35% influence awarded on army success — the Wise know how to lead.
{=taom_faction_kingdom_of_imladris_perk_1_desc}+20% village hearth growth and -15% party food consumption.
{=taom_faction_kingdom_of_imladris_perk_2_desc}+10% party speed in forest — the trees of Imladris part for their kin.

{=taom_faction_kingdom_of_lasgalen_desc}Thranduil's Woodland Realm in northern Mirkwood. Silvan archers and veteran militia hold the great forest against spider, orc, and shadow. Woodland Sustenance keeps the supplies light; Woodland Bonds keep morale high. Forest isolation slows growth.
{=taom_faction_kingdom_of_lasgalen_perk_0_desc}+10% party speed in forest and -15% food consumption.
{=taom_faction_kingdom_of_lasgalen_perk_1_desc}+25% chance militia recruits arrive as veterans.
{=taom_faction_kingdom_of_lasgalen_perk_2_desc}+3 party morale — Silvan elves march with songs.

{=taom_faction_kingdom_of_lothlorien_desc}The Golden Wood, realm of Lady Galadriel and Lord Celeborn. Wardens of Lorien defend the mallorn-forests cheaply; Lembas Bread sustains every march; Elven Harmony keeps morale unshakable. Timeless Craft means every change is slow.
{=taom_faction_kingdom_of_lothlorien_perk_0_desc}+10% party speed in forest and -20% garrison wage.
{=taom_faction_kingdom_of_lothlorien_perk_1_desc}-15% party food consumption — one bite carries a marching elf a day.
{=taom_faction_kingdom_of_lothlorien_perk_2_desc}+3 party morale and +0.5 loyalty per day in every settlement.
{=taom_faction_kingdom_of_lothlorien_su_2_desc}Heavy Elven guardian of the Golden Wood.

{=taom_faction_kingdom_of_moria_desc}The orc-host that holds the deep places of the Misty Mountains — the black pits of Moria, won from the Dwarves, and the cold peaks from Caradhras to Methedras. Larger and better-armed than the goblin rabble of the High Pass, they muster vast war-hosts for almost no influence and march hungry but tireless across the snows.
{=taom_faction_kingdom_of_moria_perk_0_desc}Army recruitment costs 40% less influence — the orc-host needs no consensus to march.
{=taom_faction_kingdom_of_moria_perk_1_desc}+30% party size and +10% speed on snow — large war-hosts bred to the cold peaks.
{=taom_faction_kingdom_of_moria_perk_2_desc}A war-host of this size eats greedily — +15% party food consumption.
{=taom_faction_kingdom_of_moria_su_0_desc}Heavier orc infantry of the deep halls.
{=taom_faction_kingdom_of_moria_su_1_desc}Bow-orc of the deep halls and high tunnels.
{=taom_faction_kingdom_of_moria_su_2_desc}Raider bred in the dark of Khazad-dûm.
{=taom_faction_kingdom_of_neldoreth_desc}An Elven realm in the northern reaches of Mirkwood, where the Wood-elves maintain their ancient forests against the creeping darkness from the south.
{=taom_faction_kingdom_of_rhudaur_desc}The wild hill country of Rhudaur, easternmost of Arnor's successor kingdoms. Fell under the influence of Angmar and its hill-men serve the Witch-king.
{=taom_faction_kingdom_of_rohan_bonus_2}-15% mounted troop wages (Riders of the Mark)
{=taom_faction_kingdom_of_rohan_bonus_3}+10% party speed on plains (Riders of the Plains)
{=taom_faction_kingdom_of_rohan_bonus_6}-10% party speed when over 50% infantry (Cavalry Dependent)

{=taom_faction_kingdom_of_rohan_desc}The Riddermark of the Horse-lords. Horse-lord Heritage cheapens every mounted recruit and upgrade; Riders of the Mark cuts mounted wages; Horse-lord Fellowship binds the Mark in loyalty. Cavalry Dependent — parties heavy with infantry slow to a crawl.
{=taom_faction_kingdom_of_rohan_perk_0_desc}-15% cost to recruit AND upgrade mounted troops — the Mark trains riders cheaply.
{=taom_faction_kingdom_of_rohan_perk_1_desc}-15% mounted troop wages and +10% party speed on plains.
{=taom_faction_kingdom_of_rohan_perk_2_desc}+5 party morale and +0.5 settlement loyalty per day.
{=taom_faction_kingdom_of_rohan_weakness_2}Helm's Deep is exposed when the Mark rides out
{=taom_faction_overlordship_of_dol_guldur_bonus_4}+1 Merchant + 1 Artisan + 13 Gang Leader notables in Dol Guldur town (20 total)

{=taom_faction_overlordship_of_dol_guldur_desc}The Necromancer's southern hold in Mirkwood. Shadow Command rallies hordes at almost no influence; Dark Conscription drills militia veterans; Shadow Captains swell the one town to twenty notables. Voracious Hordes eat as much as they slay.
{=taom_faction_overlordship_of_dol_guldur_perk_0_desc}Army influence cost reduced by 50% — dread compels obedience.
{=taom_faction_overlordship_of_dol_guldur_perk_1_desc}+20% party size and +20% volunteer respawn rate.
{=taom_faction_overlordship_of_dol_guldur_perk_2_desc}Dol Guldur's single town fields 20 notables — a 15 Gang Leader recruitment hub.
{=taom_faction_overlordship_of_gundabad_bonus_6}+1 Artisan + 3 Gang Leader notables per town (Bone-Smiths, Pale Warband Chieftains)

{=taom_faction_overlordship_of_gundabad_desc}Mount Gundabad, sacred to the Pale Orcs of Bolg's lineage. Vast warbands march from the high passes — Orc Horde discipline rallies hosts for almost no influence, Mountain Marauders rule the snows, and Plunder Demands keep every warlord paid.
{=taom_faction_overlordship_of_gundabad_perk_0_desc}Army influence cost reduced by 40% — dread compels obedience.
{=taom_faction_overlordship_of_gundabad_perk_1_desc}+20% party size limit and +10% party speed on snow.
{=taom_faction_overlordship_of_gundabad_perk_2_desc}+3 Gang Leader and +1 Artisan notable per town — recruitment swells with raiders.
{=taom_faction_overlordship_of_gundabad_weakness_2}Dwarves and Elves hate the Pale Orcs
{=taom_faction_remnants_of_angmar_desc}The dread realm of the Witch-king of Angmar in the far north. From his fortress of Carn Dum, the Witch-king wages war upon the remnants of Arnor.
{=taom_faction_stewardship_of_gondor_bonus_0}+10% party speed on plains (Men of the Fields)
{=taom_faction_stewardship_of_gondor_bonus_5}+1 settlement loyalty per day (Tower Guard Discipline)

{=taom_faction_stewardship_of_gondor_desc}The last bastion of the Dunedain in the south. Tower Guard hold the line, Gondorian Discipline rallies armies cheaply, and the Men of the Fields march on plains. War-Depleted Lands grow slowly — but Gondor stands.
{=taom_faction_stewardship_of_gondor_perk_0_desc}-20% garrison wage and +1 settlement loyalty per day.
{=taom_faction_stewardship_of_gondor_perk_1_desc}+5 party morale and +30% army influence awarded on success.
{=taom_faction_stewardship_of_gondor_perk_2_desc}+10% party speed on plains and +2.5% party size — the Pelennor is open ground.
{=taom_faction_stronghold_of_ered_gwaer_desc}A region dominated by savage Orc tribes from the eastern mountains. Fierce raiders who terrorize the borderlands between Khand and Harad.
{=taom_faction_stronghold_of_narager_desc}A desolate eastern region overrun by Orc tribes. These savage bands raid the borderlands and serve as scouts for the forces of darkness.
{=taom_faction_taskralan_of_harwan_bonus_0}+10% party speed on desert (Sons of the Sun)
{=taom_faction_taskralan_of_harwan_bonus_2}-30% caravan build cost + -10% trade penalty (Aserai Trader, inherited)
{=taom_faction_taskralan_of_harwan_bonus_3}No speed penalty on desert (Aserai Desert, inherited)

{=taom_faction_taskralan_of_harwan_desc}The Haradrim of Harwan, sons of the sun. Aserai desert resilience inherited; TAOM's Sons of the Sun add +10% party speed on desert; Haradrim Warbands add party size on top of the inherited caravan economy. Mumakil rule the southern plains.
{=taom_faction_taskralan_of_harwan_perk_0_desc}+10% party speed on desert — born to burning sands.
{=taom_faction_taskralan_of_harwan_perk_1_desc}+5% party size limit — tribal warbands ride together to Mordor's call.
{=taom_faction_taskralan_of_harwan_perk_2_desc}Inherited Aserai Trader (-30% caravans, -10% trade penalty) and Aserai Desert (no desert speed penalty); +5% daily wages.
{=taom_faction_wildmen_of_enedwaith_desc}The wild lands of Enedwaith between Arnor and Gondor. Home to scattered clans of Men who answer to no king, living as hunters and herders.

{=taom_str_culture_description.goblin}The Goblins of the High Pass are a teeming, vicious rabble dwelling in the warrens of Goblin-town. Led by their Great Goblin and petty captains, they raid the mountain roads without end, driven by greed and an ancient hatred of the Free Peoples.
{=taom_hideout_desc_goblin}Beneath the crags of the High Pass you find a reeking warren of goblins burrowed deep into the bare rock.

{=taom_str_culture_description.mistymountainorcs}The Orcs of the Misty Mountains are a brutal and numberless host of the high peaks. Led by their warlords, they wage endless raids on the lands below, relentless in their cruelty and their hunger for conquest.
{=taom_hideout_desc_mistymountainorcs}Beneath the crags of the Misty Mountains you find a foul warren of orcs burrowed into the bare rock.

{=taom_str_culture_description.lindon}Lindon, the Grey Havens, is a refuge of wisdom and beauty led by Cirdan the Shipwright. Set on the shores of the Gulf of Lune, its people are loremasters and guardians of Middle-earth's ancient knowledge. The Elves of Lindon offer counsel and aid to those who stand against the darkness, preserving the light of hope and unity.

{=taom_str_culture_description.bluecraig}The Goblins of the Ered Luin are a teeming, vicious rabble dwelling in the warrens of Blue Craig. Led by their Great Goblin and petty captains, they raid the mountain roads without end, driven by greed and an ancient hatred of the Free Peoples.
